notes.text: Last full day: suitcases are already on their way to Haneda T3, so every tax-free buy goes in your carry-on, unused, with its receipt, ready for the customs kiosk tomorrow.
Year-end closures start around now: check Instagram for the small Koenji and Nakano shops before you go; chains, Donki and clubs run as normal.
Original passports (ATOM checks, Donki tax-free needs your own), warm layers: it's cold and dark by the time you reach Harajuku.

stops.summary: Shinjuku's historic tempura house at lunch prices: the one classic Japanese sit-down meal of the trip.
stops.story: Tsunahachi has been frying tempura in Shinjuku for generations, and this branch takes bookings, so all 8 can sit down to crisp prawns and vegetables straight from the oil. Lunch sets are the budget way into what is a proper old-Tokyo meal.
how: Book ahead: for 8 or more, contact the shop directly (TableCheck for smaller bookings, 03-3358-2788 for questions).
Order the lunch sets; the tempura and sashimi course is ¥3,850.
Leave by 12:35 for the 12:49 Chuo rapid to Koenji (¥200).
tips: The 10% service charge applies at dinner, another reason to come at lunch.
Online availability for the trip dates wasn't confirmed, so get a booking confirmation in writing.
stops.booking: For 8 or more, contact the shop directly; TableCheck for online booking
wishes: We love to do it all

stops.summary: Tokyo's best vintage digging: cheaper, rougher and more varied than Shimokitazawa, with almost no tourists.
stops.story: Koenji is where locals now go for vintage: covered arcades stuffed with tiny shops, bargain racks spilling onto the pavement, and punk and designer-archive dens in the Kita-Kore Building. It's rougher and cheaper than Shimokitazawa, and the hunt is half the fun.
how: Chuo rapid Shinjuku → Koenji, 12:49→12:55; it only stops at Koenji on weekdays, which today is.
Walk south down Pal into Look arcade toward Shin-Koenji, then cross to the north side for Kita-Kore.
Split into 2–3 groups and meet back at the station.
tips: Dig the ¥500–1,000 bargain racks before the main rails.
Kita-Kore closes earlier than the rest (11:00–18:00), so don't leave it to last.
Some indie shops close irregularly at year-end: check their Instagram.
wishes: We love to do it all

stops.summary: A 1960s arcade crammed with Mandarake: figures, retro toys, cards and idol goods, calmer than Akihabara.
stops.story: Nakano Broadway looks like an ordinary 1960s shopping arcade until you climb to floors 2–4, where Mandarake branches and tiny collector shops sell everything from vintage robots to trading cards and idol goods. It's the otaku treasure house locals prefer to Akihabara: calmer and often cheaper.
how: JR Chuo line Koenji → Nakano, 15:17→15:19 (¥160), then walk up Sun Mall.
Head straight to floors 2–4.
Go in two groups; the corridors are narrow.
tips: Figures and cards start from ¥500, so set yourselves a budget.
Keep an eye on the clock: the Fuunji queue starts before 17:00.
wishes: We love to do it all

stops.summary: Tokyo's benchmark tsukemen: thick noodles dipped in dense chicken-and-fish broth, worth the queue.
stops.story: Fuunji's tsukemen is the bowl other Tokyo shops get measured against: chewy, thick noodles you dip into a heavy, smoky chicken-and-fish broth. It's a tiny counter shop where the line forms well before opening, and one of the few famous Shinjuku ramen queues that's genuinely worth it.
how: Chuo rapid Nakano → Shinjuku, 16:39→16:43 (¥200), then walk from the South Exit.
Get in the queue for the 17:00 dinner opening.
Order the tokusei tsukemen; you'll be seated in waves at the counter.
tips: No reservations, and the soup can sell out, so don't arrive late.
A late-2025 visitor found more than 50 people in line by 11:15 at lunch: the dinner opening is the smarter slot.
Tsukemen is ¥1,000; ramen is ¥950 if anyone prefers soup.
wishes: We love to do it all

stops.summary: After-dark streetwear run: Takeshita, the Ura-Hara back lanes, then Cat Street's sneaker shops toward Shibuya.
stops.story: This is the streetwear and sneaker spine of Tokyo: Takeshita's crepe stands, Ura-Hara's lanes of brand flagships and consignment shops like L.A. Avenue, then Cat Street with atmos, Kicks Lab and 2nd Street. In late December it's already dark, the shop windows glow and the crowds are thinner than by day.
how: JR Yamanote Yoyogi → Harajuku, 18:12→18:15 (¥160).
Quick pass down Takeshita for a crepe, then cross Meiji-dori into Ura-Hara.
Walk Cat Street south: atmos and Kicks Lab first, 2nd Street last as it closes later.
tips: Most shops shut at 20:00 (2nd Street at 21:00), so hit the must-buys first.
Set one meet point: Harajuku station, Omotesando exit.
Ask for tax-free and pay on your own passport; keep it unused in your carry-on.
wishes: We love to do it all

stops.summary: The final take-home haul at Tokyo's biggest 24-hour Donki: snacks, KitKats, cosmetics and costumes.
stops.story: MEGA Donki Shibuya is a multi-floor maze of snacks, KitKat flavours, cosmetics, costumes, character goods and cheap electronics, with the jingle on a loop. It's the easy place for tax-free shopping now, since Don Quijote waives the refund fee.
how: Hanzomon line Omotesando → Shibuya, 20:34→20:36 (¥180).
Split into pairs and set a meet-up time at the entrance.
Each person pays on their own passport, aiming for ¥5,000 ex-tax on one receipt for the refund.
tips: Purchases can't be pooled: everyone pays separately.
Pack tax-free goods unused, with receipts, in your carry-on for the customs kiosk at Haneda T3 tomorrow.
The refund is fee-free unless you take it as cash at the airport.
wishes: We love to do it all

stops.summary: The last big night: Shibuya's young three-floor club, open even on a Monday, with cheap early entry.
stops.story: ATOM is the young mainstream club of Shibuya: three floors, room for 800 and open every night, which makes it the party on a Monday when the bigger clubs are dark. Get in early and the first drink is basically free.
how: Walk up Dogenzaka to Maruyamacho (6 min).
Be in before 23:30 for men ¥900 / women ¥400, 1 drink included.
Original passports at the door; no jerseys, sport pants or sandals.
tips: After 23:30 it's men ¥2,900 / women ¥900, so don't linger at Donki.
Visible tattoos can get you turned away.
When you're done, take 2 taxis to Shinjuku 3-chome (20 min).
stops.booking: Walk in; arrive early for the cheap rate
wishes: We want to maximise all the time we've got in the country

stops.summary: Grill-your-own scallops and highballs at a 24-hour seafood izakaya: the trip's last feed.
stops.story: Isomaru Suisan puts a little grill on your table and you cook scallops, crab-miso shells and squid yourself, with cheap highballs alongside. At this hour it's the after-party and the last supper of the trip in one, over four floors with room for a group of 8.
how: Taxi from Shibuya to Shinjuku 3-chome.
Ask for a table for 8; it's easy off-peak.
Order scallops and crab-miso shells for the grill, then highballs.
tips: A 10% late-night surcharge applies at this hour.
Course menus need booking the day before; just order à la carte.
stops.cost: about ¥2,500–4,000 pp with drinks (+10% late-night surcharge)
wishes: We want to maximise all the time we've got in the country
